text_blocks.snippet: Heart disease research encompasses a wide range of studies aimed at understanding, preventing, and treating cardiovascular diseases. These studies often involve large-scale, long-term investigations like the Framingham Heart Study, which has followed multiple generations to identify risk factors and improve prevention strategies. Cardiology, the field focused on heart and cardiovascular system disorders, utilizes these studies to diagnose and treat conditions like coronary artery disease, heart failure, and congenital heart defects.
snippet_highlighted_words: encompasses a wide range of studies aimed at understanding, preventing, and treating cardiovascular diseases

text_blocks.snippet: Here's a more detailed look at heart disease research:

list.title: Framingham Heart Study:
list.snippet: This landmark study, ongoing for over 75 years, has significantly shaped our understanding of heart disease risk factors and prevention strategies. It has expanded to investigate the impact of gut microbes on heart health and utilizes advanced technologies like AI and omics, according to the National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute (NHLBI).

list.title: Cardiovascular Health Study (CHS):
list.snippet: Focused on adults aged 65 and older, the CHS aims to identify risk factors for heart disease and stroke, according to the National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute (NHLBI). It has also explored other age-related conditions like dementia and kidney disease.

list.title: Coronary Artery Risk Development in Young Adults (CARDIA) Study:
list.snippet: This study examines factors that contribute to heart disease development starting in young adulthood, a period before the onset of clinical symptoms.

list.title: Strong Heart Study (SHS):
list.snippet: Investigates cardiovascular disease in American Indian communities, including genetic factors through the Strong Heart Family Study.

list.title: SPRINT Study:
list.snippet: Found that intensive blood pressure treatment in older adults reduces heart events and mortality.

list.title: RAID Trial:
list.snippet: Showed that a drug for angina can reduce the risk of dangerous heart rhythms.

list.title: Semaglutide for Heart Failure:
list.snippet: Research in the New England Journal of Medicine suggests that semaglutide can improve quality of life for heart failure patients and reduce cardiovascular risks in those with obesity and cardiovascular disease.

list.title: PRESS (Platelet Reactivity ExpreSs Score):
list.snippet: A tool developed to assess platelet reactivity and identify individuals who might benefit from antiplatelet therapy.

list.title: EKO DUO System:
list.snippet: The Mayo Clinic is evaluating the diagnostic accuracy of the EKO DUO System in detecting genetic heart diseases.

list.title: Mortality Rates:
list.snippet: While heart disease mortality rates have decreased significantly in the US, disparities persist, particularly among those with lower incomes and less education.

list.title: Disparities:
list.snippet: A recent study revealed widening heart disease disparities in the US, with lower-income individuals facing significantly higher risks of various cardiovascular conditions.

list.title: Lifestyle Factors:
list.snippet: Research continues to explore the impact of lifestyle choices, including diet and physical activity, on heart health.
